operator_locked_immediate_priorities: P0-A: normal nonterminal turn worktime at least 10 minutes (600 observed elapsed seconds)
P0-B: SAME MAIN final scheduler write uses full recurring VEVENT and targets observed close + exactly 1 minute (60 seconds)

active_retest.purpose: Test whether the minimal proven same-automation full-RRULE update pattern eliminates post-close overwrite of the desired low-idle due.
active_retest.success_signal: After a nonterminal close, live metadata retains SAME MAIN enabled=true with RRULE:FREQ=HOURLY and DTSTART equal to observed close + exactly 1 minute (60 seconds), with no later same-wake schedule mutation.
active_retest.failure_signal: The 11-minute (660-second) provisional or another stale/derived due remains after close, RRULE disappears, automation is disabled/replaced, or a post-final reconciliation mutates schedule again.

latest_diagnosis.evidence: A separate RRULE self-update test repeatedly preserves the same automation, enabled state, and recurring RRULE while moving DTSTART. MAIN used the same schedule shape but durable/control reconciliation could leave a later provisional due as final state.
latest_diagnosis.implication: Make the live close-time full-RRULE update authoritative and last; make durable state follow it rather than drive another scheduler mutation.

next_corrective_experiment.hypothesis: Minimal same-automation full recurring VEVENT updates plus last-writer-wins close semantics will preserve the close + 1 minute (60 seconds) due and reduce idle without new scheduler machinery.
